"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/count-connected-components-in-lcm-graph/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

3378. Count Connected Components in LCM Graph

You are given an array of integers nums of size n and a positive integer threshold.

There is a graph consisting of n nodes with the i-th node having a value of nums[i]. Two nodes i and j in the graph are connected via an undirected edge if lcm(nums[i], nums[j]) <= threshold.

Return the number of connected components in this graph.

A connected component is a subgraph of a graph in which there exists a path between any two vertices, and no vertex of the subgraph shares an edge with a vertex outside of the subgraph.

The term lcm(a, b) denotes the least common multiple of a and b.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [2,4,8,3,9], threshold = 5
Output: 4
Explanation:
The four connected components are (2, 4), (3), (8), (9).

Example 2:

Input: nums = [2,4,8,3,9,12], threshold = 10
Output: 2
Explanation:
The two connected components are (2, 3, 4, 8, 9), and (12).

Constraints:

    1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
    1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
    All elements of nums are unique.
    1 <= threshold <= 2 * 10^5
"""


class Solution:
    def countComponents(self, nums: List[int], threshold: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        # map value to index
        val_to_idx = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(nums)}
        parent = list(range(n))
        size = [1] * n

        def find(x: int) -> int:
            while parent[x] != x:
                parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
                x = parent[x]
            return x

        def union(a: int, b: int) -> bool:
            ra = find(a)
            rb = find(b)
            if ra == rb:
                return False
            if size[ra] < size[rb]:
                ra, rb = rb, ra
            parent[rb] = ra
            size[ra] += size[rb]
            return True

        # initial components count
        components = n

        # Values > threshold cannot have lcm <= threshold with any positive integer,
        # so they are isolated; we simply won't connect them.
        # Build buckets: for each t in [1..threshold], bucket[t] lists indices i
        # such that nums[i] divides t. Then any pair in bucket[t] has lcm <= t <= threshold.
        if threshold >= 1:
            buckets = [[] for _ in range(threshold + 1)]
            for v, idx in val_to_idx.items():
                if v <= threshold:
                    step = v
                    t = step
                    # add index to every multiple t of v up to threshold
                    while t <= threshold:
                        buckets[t].append(idx)
                        t += step

            # union all indices in each bucket
            for t in range(1, threshold + 1):
                bucket = buckets[t]
                if len(bucket) <= 1:
                    continue
                first = bucket[0]
                for other in bucket[1:]:
                    if union(first, other):
                        components -= 1

        return components


sol = Solution()

print(sol.countComponents([2, 4, 8, 3, 9], 5))  # 4

assert sol.countComponents([2, 4, 8, 3, 9], 5) == 4
assert sol.countComponents([2, 4, 8, 3, 9, 12], 10) == 2

assert sol.countComponents([7], 7) == 1
assert sol.countComponents([4, 6], 12) == 1
assert sol.countComponents([4, 9], 12) == 2
assert sol.countComponents([2, 2, 3, 3], 6) == 3
assert sol.countComponents([-1, -2, -3], 0) == 3
assert sol.countComponents([1, 200000], 200000) == 1
assert sol.countComponents([10, 11, 12], 5) == 3
assert sol.countComponents([1000000000, 999999937, 2], 3) == 3
assert sol.countComponents(list(range(1, 16)), 15) == 1
assert sol.countComponents([2, 3, 4, 9], 12) == 1
